newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FOCUS - Dutch Vendex 96/97 profit up, demerger ahead.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Dutch Vendex 96/97 profit up, demerger ahead.

text.p: Dutch retailing and services group Vendex International reported a 30 percent jump in net profits to 539 million guilders ($277.1 million) on Tuesday, and further detailed its plans to split into two separate arms.
The headline profits were in line with expectations, but operating profit excluding income from the development and sale of property was just below forecasts at 362 million guilders.
Vendex said it intended to place and list shares worth 600 million guilders of the new group Vedior N.V. by an initial public offering (IPO) in the middle of 1997.
"Call it May, June," chairman of the board Jan-Michiel Hessels said.
Hessels said he was confident the planned demerger of the services activities from Vendex's retailing core, announced in January, would work out positively for both arms.
"After the demerger, both companies will have a very strong position for further growth," he said.
After the IPO, Vendex's current shareholders will receive the remaining Vedior shares as soon as technically possible, Hessels said, adding this would likely take at least 90 days.
He said the demerger was going according to the plan, but the company was still awaiting government approval of the law permitting such operations.

"We expect the split to be finalised at the beginning of 1998, depending on the moment at which changes in the law on the split of legal entities will become valid, or the obtaining of an earlier ruling by the Ministry of Finance," Vendex earlier said in a statement.

Hessels said the demerger would help Vendex's food retail unit pursue further acquisitions, mainly in the Netherlands. "There's only a limited number of players on the market. We are now better positioned for further growth."

The group recently strengthened its foothold in the specialty stores segment with the acquisition of sports footware and clothing chain Scapino and the opticians chain of the Optische Exploitatie Maatschappij.
Operating income of the retail activities rose 29 percent to 352 million guilders. Excluding property income, it was up 50 percent to 247 million guilders.

Within the retail trade division, the food group increased its 'pure' operating income (excluding property) by 39 percent to 117 million guilders. Longer opening hours in the Netherlands gave a push to turnover at the specialty and department stores.

Department stores also benefited from favourable fashion business pushing the 'pure' operating income at the department stores 75 percent higher to 56 million guilders. At Vendex's specialty stores it was up 51 percent to 74 million guilders.
The future Vedior business services arm, which focuses on commercial cleaning and temporary employment, increased operating profit excluding property by 14 percent to 129 million guilders.

Within the division, temporary employment operating income was up 19 percent at 75 million guilders in 1996/1997. French temp employment agency BIS, acquired earlier this year, posted a 106 million franc ($18.2 million) loss in 1996.
Vendex board member Gert Smit said results of BIS had been positive during the first two months of 1997.
"We expect BIS to give a positive contribution to the group's results in 1997," Hessels said.

Once demerged, Vedior aims for cross-border expansion in order to be able to compete for major international customers, board member Gert Smit said, adding that a major player has to be present in all big European countries in order to be able to offer major contracts.

Vendex announced a dividend of two guilders, up from 1.50 a year ago and repeated a previous profit forecast for the year ahead, saying it aimed to maintain an annual average profit rise of at least 10 percent.
Hessels said property-related income, 111 million guilders of the operating profit in 1996/97, would remain substantial for the next couple of years.
Vendex shares rose to 92.50 guilders before easing back to 91.10 guilders at 1210 GMT, twenty cents above Monday's close.
